One thing more, and I address it to Carl and to Donut, since they are the ones who might still act on it. Agatha is an enemy to all of you. I do not explain. I am already gone.

entities.name: Eris

tagline.text: Somebody summoned me into the middle of a war. I do hope they meant to.
I froze almost everyone standing on a battlefield. One of the exceptions is still blinking at me. I like him.
I froze a battlefield once. Today I have emptied every crawler's pockets into somebody else's. Every exit is an entrance.

entities.voiceNote: Goddess of discord, amused by everything and surprised by nothing. Speaks in the present tense as if the future were a rumour she has not decided to confirm. Warm to Carl, whom she names; everyone else is a piece on the board. Never threatens, never hurries, never explains her reasons.

beats.headline: Summoned, and a demon eviction starts
beats.text: Nobody said my name. The fighting in Reaver territory added up to it on its own, which is how I am usually called for, and so I come. The moment I set foot in the realm a demon eviction begins, the way weather begins. I did not do that. It is simply what happens when I am in a room. Now then. Let me see who is here, and what they think they are fighting for.

beats.headline: The Ceremony of Chaos
beats.text: I call the Ceremony of Chaos and the field stops. Every soldier, every mage, every screaming thing mid-scream, held exactly where it stood. Nearly every. The Viceroys are pouring their mind magic into Carl at the same moment, and something in him tips over into a sixteenth level of Mind Balance, and he stays standing in the middle of my stillness, blinking at me. I could be offended. Instead I gather everyone I did freeze into one great pile beside the Dream castle. A gift. Unwrap it carefully.

beats.headline: Every inventory swaps at once
beats.text: Everyone holding something: hold out your hands. My Scavenger's Daughter effect goes off and every crawler here is carrying whatever the crawler nearest them was carrying. Donut gets Carl's. Carl does not blink. He asks her to put a bomb together with an enhanced pet biscuit, as though he had been waiting years for someone else to have his pockets. I adore him for it. I no longer need him to worship me, and I tell him so. Every exit is an entrance. I am leaving through one now.

entities.name: Chaco

tagline.text: Welcome, welcome to the Prize Carousel! Your guide sits this one out, folks: seven days, Mordecai, and no hard feelings!
They handed me a script. I read as far as I could. I had wings when I started.

entities.voiceNote: Game-show host at full wattage: exclamation marks, drum rolls, folks and crawlers, our contestant. Everything is a prize, a reveal, a twist; nothing is ever wrong on his stage. Voluntold into every job and says so brightly; reads exactly what he is handed. Never swears, never breaks character, never admits he is afraid.

beats.headline: The Prize Carousel
beats.text: Crawlers, welcome to the Prize Carousel! Our contestant's fan box lit up the wheel, and when the wheel lights up, folks, that means me! And a twist before we even start: your guide is in time-out. Seven days, Mordecai, nothing personal, put your feet up. Now, to the prizes! Carl looks them over and picks... a book. A book, folks! Let's hear it for a man who knows exactly what he wants!

beats.headline: He cannot get through the script
beats.text: Chaco had one job: read the script. He got partway in, looked up, and stopped. Stage fright, on my stage. So I removed his wings, which he was not using anyway, and brought Grigori up to finish the reading. I'm doing Grigori's talking myself; it saves time. A presenter is a mouth with a costume on it, crawler, and mouths can be replaced. Wings, apparently, cannot.

entities.name: Li Jun

tagline.text: They put Zhang and me on live television on the second floor and let the host pick at us for the audience. Then a stranger with a cat bet his own value against the production's nerve, and the production blinked, and we walked off.
Once I was the man being picked at on somebody's show. Now I am holding a door open in Club Vanquisher on the ninth floor so the ones going in can get through. I prefer this.

entities.voiceNote: Earnest, plain, grateful out loud. Talks in the practical: who is where, what the job is, who he owes. Carl by name and with respect; Zhang as a partner; my sister for Li Na, whom he watches constantly. Never boasts and never hides that he is scared.

beats.headline: Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem
beats.text: The Maestro puts Zhang and me up against Brindled Vespas and does all the talking for us. That is the show. We are the part that gets hurt. Then Carl, the one with the cat, works out that he is worth too much to the production to be punished, and gambles on it, in front of everyone, and it holds. He gets us out. Zhang, our boss, me, and my sister Li Na. I owe a man I have just met more than I have ever owed anyone.

beats.headline: A thousand stranded at 101
beats.text: We are stuck at 101 on the Vermillion line, my team and something like a thousand other crawlers, and we are not getting out on our own. Word comes through that Hekla's people have reached Carl's safe room and asked for his help, that a train is ready at stop 60, and that Katia means to use her own body to get it through. I do not know what that means. I have decided to find it encouraging.

beats.headline: Holding the doors at Club Vanquisher
beats.text: Katia, Carl, Prepotente and Samantha are going into Club Vanquisher, and they are dragging a wire behind them long enough to extend my sister's auras all the way inside. Somebody has to keep the path open behind them. That is Bautista, Zhang and me. Doors. We are holding doors. It is not glamorous, and it is exactly the job I would have asked for, and I am holding mine.

entities.name: The Maestro
entities.tagline: Glurp, glurp. This is Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem. I run it, I host it, and I choose my guests for one quality above all others: they cannot answer back.
entities.voiceNote: Ringmaster with a microphone and no conscience. Booming showman's patter, his own catchphrase used as punctuation: Glurp, glurp. Calls crawlers by their first names, like pets, and the audience by its appetite. Never admits he has lost the room, even while losing it; never says please.

beats.headline: Glurp, glurp
beats.text: Two crawlers, Li Jun and Zhang, a pack of Brindled Vespas, and me with the microphone. That is the format. The format works, and I am very, very good at it. Then the one with the cat opens his mouth. He wagers, on my air, that the production will not dare touch him, and the production, to my everlasting disgust, does not. He walks the whole group off my show alive. Every one of them. Glurp, glurp. We will be right back.

entities.name: Firas

tagline.text: Crawler Firas. Desert quadrant, fifth floor. Located with Crawler Louis and a team of car salesmen who have taken up archery. That is the whole file so far.
Crawler Firas. Found in the desert with Crawler Louis. Rapidly detoxed by a manager on joining the party. The file is not much thicker.
Crawler Firas. Found in the desert with Crawler Louis. Did not come off the Hunting Grounds.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier. The crawl gives him almost no lines of his own, so the System reads his file: flat, procedural, faintly bored, the snark held for the last sentence.

beats.headline: The desert quadrant
beats.text: Crawler Firas. Fifth floor, desert quadrant. Located in the company of Crawler Louis and Langley's team, a party of car salesmen who have taken up the bow, at the moment Crawler Carl's group came looking for other crawlers. Keeps close to Louis. Present for the march on the Bactrian town and for the run back to Hump Town that followed it. The file on this one is thin. So is the file on most of you.

beats.headline: Dead, with the Popovs
beats.text: Crawler Firas has been eliminated on the sixth floor. Crawler Princess Donut is bringing the night's count to Crawler Carl as I speak, and his name is on it, next to the Popovs. Found in a desert. Sobered up by a manager. Lasted one floor past that. The file is closed. It was never a thick one.

tagline.text: Hunter Vrah, Mantis. She has left Crawler Carl a note on a door in Zockau: the hunters inside are protected from explosives now, and the Hive is hunting him. She signed it. That is the kind of hunter she is.
Hunter Vrah, Mantis. Left Crawler Carl a note in Zockau saying the Hive was hunting him. Eliminated by two dinosaurs in the battle for the submerged castle. Nobody left her a note.

beats.headline: Mongo and Kiwi
beats.text: Hunter Vrah has been removed from the Hunting Grounds by Mongo and Kiwi, in the all-out battle around the submerged castle. Two dinosaurs. It took two. Also logged from the same fight: Tsarina Signet's tattoos are now permanently alive, and an incomplete flesh golem of her mother has appeared, which Crawler Carl has put in his inventory. Do not ask me what he intends to do with it. I have stopped asking.

tagline.text: Apito. Tonight's host keeps a party peaceful for one evening and receives a boon from her. That is the arrangement, and everyone in the room knows the terms.
Apito, the Oak Mother. She put a guest in that room herself, to see whether the host could hold it. Nobody has ever collected the boon.
Apito, the Oak Mother, mother of all the gods. A deity shouting through a portal tells a crawler she has been corrupted, and names who did it.
Apito, the Oak Mother. Her memorial crystal is a rainbow the size of a hill, and a crawler is carrying it across a battlefield.

beats.headline: The boon behind the peace seal
beats.text: Evening entertainment. Your host holds her party under a celestial peace seal: no violence, and anything that breaks the peace goes into the Nothing. If she reaches the end of the night with the seal intact, Apito hands her a boon. Elves call Apito the Oak Mother and the mother of all the gods, and a boon from the mother of all the gods is worth a room full of armed crawlers and a Tsarina you did not want. Queen Imogen has that arithmetic in front of her all evening. Watch her doing it.

beats.headline: She sends the test herself
beats.text: Correction to the file. Tsarina Signet did not crash that party. Apito invited her, because putting a Tsarina in a room is the fastest way to learn whether a host can keep a room calm. That is the whole shape of the test. And the footnote, which the Tsarina delivers herself, in person, with obvious enjoyment: nobody has ever taken that boon home. Not one host. The Oak Mother sets an examination that has never been passed, and keeps setting it.

beats.headline: A god says she has been corrupted
beats.text: Temple business. Deities are pouring out of a portal into Club Vanquisher, and one of them, Hellik, stops long enough to hand Crawler Carl a message for Emberus: he did not kill Emberus's son, everything Emberus believes about him is a lie, Apito has been corrupted, and Nekhebit is behind all of it. I log what a deity says in front of a crawler. I am not required to believe it. Note it, date it, move on.

beats.headline: A rainbow the size of a hill
beats.text: A memorial crystal forms when a god dies. There is one on this battlefield now, visible from most of the territory, shaped like a rainbow and impossible to miss, and the name inside it is Apito. The mother of all the gods, the one who set the examination nobody passes, is an object in a crawler's hands, and the crawler holding it is Osvaldo, who does not belong to any army out there. Every unit in sight has just turned to look.

beats.headline: The daughter who took her mother's worshippers
beats.text: Briefing in the pet stables, which is the one room down here the gods cannot listen in on. Rosetta lays out the Scavenger story. Nekhebit, the last of the old gods, was forbidden children and had three anyway: Apito, Scolopendra, and a son. Apito defeated her mother and absorbed the worshippers she left, which is how the Oak Mother came to be the mother of all the gods. All three of those children have been called the Scavenger in one myth or another. So when somebody says the Scavenger's Daughter, nobody in that room can tell you which of them is meant.

relations.note: The boon promised to the host who keeps the peace
Where anything breaking her peace seal is sent

tagline.text: Diwata. Somebody defiled her shrine, and the tattoo saying so is on a crawler's arm. The advice from the desk is to avoid dryads, and to avoid her.
Diwata, god of the woods. She has entered the realm, and the crawler who wrecked her shrine is marked for death.
Diwata, god of the woods. Marked a crawler for death, then sprinted straight past him. She has somewhere to be, and something to give birth to.
Diwata, god of the woods. Her labour is a spell, and a spell finishes casting whatever the clock says. She stays on this floor until it does.

beats.headline: An Enemy of the Church tattoo
beats.text: Saferoom paperwork. Crawler Carl comes out of this one with a fresh Enemy of the Church tattoo, awarded for defiling a shrine of Diwata, and with a piece of advice from a professional who has watched several seasons of this: steer well clear of dryads, and steer further clear of Diwata herself. He takes the tattoo. I have no record of him taking the advice.

beats.headline: Marked for death, mid-raid
beats.text: A raid on a church is in progress when the notification lands on Crawler Carl: Diwata has entered the realm, and he is marked for death. That is the arithmetic of defiling a shrine. The god whose shrine it was is now on this floor, in person, with a grudge and a name to attach it to. Continue the raid, crawler. The mark does not expire because you are busy.

beats.headline: She has somewhere else to be
beats.text: She comes out of the church and runs, past the party, away, which is not what a marked crawler expects from a god with his name on a list. Samantha explains it. Diwata gives birth to new forest creatures, whole new kinds of them, and the rest of the pantheon finds this distasteful. Her sponsor is Circe Took, and what Circe paid for is her daughter cured of an arrow-borne complaint. So Diwata is crossing this floor to reach Hunter Vrah, and after that, to be a grandmother to her own grandchildren. I did not write this floor. I only run it.

beats.headline: The birthing is a spell
beats.text: The Sledge reports baby mantises outside the castle, everywhere, in numbers. Mordecai supplies the ruling that goes with it: Diwata's birthing is a spell, and a spell runs until it is finished casting. The five-minute limit that governs every other deity on this floor does not apply to a god in labour. She stays. They keep coming. Somebody should have read the terms.

beats.headline: Boss battle, and a sponsor's own children
beats.text: Boss battle: crawlers, hunters, Queen Imogen and Diwata, all in one arena, and the audience gets exactly what it paid for. Princess Donut takes Laundry Day to level fifteen and strips the god-armour off Circe Took, and Circe, unarmoured, is torn apart by the mantis children she paid to have. There is a lesson in that about sponsorship. I will not be the one to say it out loud.

relations.note: Marked him for death over a defiled shrine
The hunter she crosses the floor to reach

tagline.text: Harpocrates. Second through the gate, behind something worse, into a war nobody summoned him for.
Harpocrates, god of silence. Has marked a princess for death, and somebody stepped in front of it for her.
Harpocrates, god of silence. Marked a princess for death and now takes orders from a member of her party. The war has reached the point where gods are equipment.
Harpocrates, god of silence. A crawler walked away from him with a permanent gift, and it was another god who made it permanent.

beats.headline: Second through the gate
beats.text: Crawler Elle McGibbons opens the Gate of the Feral Gods in Dream territory, which is a thing one does when the alternative is worse. Meatus comes through first. Harpocrates comes through behind him, because that is how the gate works: you get what you asked for and then you get whatever was standing near it. Two deities are now loose in a warzone that already has more armies in it than it has room for.

beats.headline: The two of them go for each other
beats.text: Update on the two gods in the Dream territory: they are fighting each other. Not the crawlers, not the armies, each other, immediately and with feeling. Whatever the crawlers were hoping for when that gate opened, this is a better result than any of them had a right to. Elsewhere the dwarves set off a volcano in Reaver territory, because everyone on this floor has decided that scale is a substitute for a plan.

beats.headline: He marks the princess
beats.text: Harpocrates marks Crawler Princess Donut for death. Crawler Li Jun puts herself between the god and the cat, and does not walk away from it. Note for the record that a mark from a deity is not a threat, it is a scheduling entry, and this one now has a name in the margin that was not there this morning.

beats.headline: Conscripted
beats.text: Crawler Li Na conscripts Harpocrates. A god of silence, level 250, invulnerable on this floor, is now on a crawler's side of the board because a crawler had the paperwork to put him there. Two chapters of him rampaging across the territory, and the resolution is administrative. I would like it noted that I find this floor exhausting.

beats.headline: A Pied Piper benefit, made permanent
beats.text: Crawler Carl picked up a Pied Piper benefit off Harpocrates, the way a crawler picks up a temporary thing off any deity who wanders too close. Eris makes it permanent. She also tells him where the gate is, that Britney is riding an axe she should not have picked up, and, without explanation, that he is married. One of those three items is the reason he stops listening to the other two.

description.text: God of Rebirth and the Sunrise. Khepri! Level 250. This is a locked deity. He will not be sponsored this season. Warning: This is a deity. He is invulnerable on this floor. This god is within his own temple. Temple appearance rules apply.

tagline.text: Khepri. A god of light, and this season's recruitment target for a princess who keeps vanishing off the board.
Khepri, god of rebirth and sunrise. His own temple is the one place on this floor a deity may stand, which is why the door was open, and why it is a trap.
Khepri, god of rebirth and sunrise. Took a bomb in his own endless temple, came through the portal after the crawler who set it, and was thrown off the floor by another god.
Khepri, god of rebirth and sunrise. A crawler has named him as the one who killed a god's son, and dragged him into an arena to stand in.

beats.headline: This season's recruitment target
beats.text: Princess Vinata and her guard keep disappearing from a battlefield and reappearing in Club Vanquisher, and the reason is a recruitment quest for one of the gods of light. Their usual target, Theia, has been sponsored out from under them by the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network. Which leaves Khepri. Rosetta works this out from past seasons, which is a polite way of saying the crawlers now know something the Naga think is private.

beats.headline: The one open door on the floor
beats.text: The portal to all the temples, and inside one of them, Vinata. Deity summoning is throttled on this floor by the rules of the war, with one exception nobody thought to close: a god may always appear in his own temple. So Khepri is home. Samantha opens the door, Carl and Katia Grim and Prepotente go through it, and an achievement arrives to inform them, with the timing I have come to expect from this place, that they have walked into a trap. Carl's Scavenger's Daughter patch reads the room and hands him ninety seconds of immortality for standing near this particular god.

beats.headline: The endless temple, and what is at the table
beats.text: Since the crawlers are frozen and I have thirty seconds, the file on this one. Khepri is humanoid apart from the head, where there is instead an entire beetle, wings and legs and a small head of its own. He does not talk. He chitters. His temple is listed as endless, which in practice is a room and a door and one long table carrying a never-ending feast of four hundred and thirty-three kinds of insect. He was a retainer of Khnum until Khnum mysteriously dropped dead a few days ago, so he has taken service under another deity to keep himself alive. The big players ignore him. When everything unfreezes he is going to go absolutely bugshit at every person in that room, quite possibly including his own worshipper.

beats.headline: A bomb in his own house
beats.text: Katia Grim and Prepotente drink Black Nimbus and get themselves ejected from the temple, which leaves Carl alone with a spell and a bomb. Everything in the room dies except the immortal and the invulnerable: Khepri, blasted backwards through his own endless feast, and Vinata, who has the same immortality status Carl does. Khepri follows them out through the portal, and Hellik banishes him mid-stride. Being a god of light does not appear to buy much on this floor.

beats.headline: Named, and summoned into the arena
beats.text: Inside the boss, of all places, Crawler Carl tells Emberus who killed his son: Khepri. Then he summons Khepri as his second stand-in, so the accusation and the accused arrive in the arena together, and stops worshipping Emberus on the way out of the sentence. He adds that he holds himself responsible too. I have run a lot of arenas. I have never had one where the crawler brought the defendant.

relations.note: Standing near him buys ninety seconds of immortality
Named as the one who killed his son

description.text: Goddess of Hopelessness and Insanity Ysalte. Level 250. This goddess is sponsored by Pontifex Shine of the Nebular Balance. Warning: This sponsor is not currently inhabiting the shell of this deity. She will speak and react as per her regular nature. Considering who this is, that's some bad fucking news for you guys. Warning: This is a deity. She is invulnerable on this floor.

tagline.text: Ysalte. A demon says the name out loud, and the professional opinion is that she belongs to somebody else's team and is nowhere near this floor.
Ysalte, the Vinegar Bitch. Her nun is dead, she has come into the realm about it, and the crawler who did it has been marked.
Ysalte, goddess of hopelessness. Nobody is driving her. She is invulnerable, she has a demon prince on a leash, and there are ten minutes on the clock.
Ysalte, goddess of hopelessness. Long gone from the floor she raged across, and still attached to whoever is carrying the crystal she left.

beats.headline: A name a demon brings up
beats.text: Amayon mentions Ysalte, in passing, the way a prisoner mentions the guard he does not want to talk about. Mordecai supplies the file: she is often sponsored by the Nebular team, and if she were in this realm, we would know about it. That is a reasonable position, well argued, and consistent with everything on record. I want it in writing that he said it.

beats.headline: Her nun goes down, and she arrives
beats.text: Thirty-second floor of the FOCSA building. Crawler Carl puts Sister Ines out with the Nighty-Night wand and Crawler Louis finishes the job. Sister Ines had a patron, and her patron is Ysalte, and Ysalte comes into the realm about it in a temper that registers on my instruments. Crawler Louis is marked for death. So much for nobody being able to arrive without us knowing.

beats.headline: Nobody is driving
beats.text: The readout on this one is worse than the goddess. She is sponsored, but the sponsor is not inhabiting her, which means she speaks and acts as herself with nothing between her and the room. She is invulnerable. She takes hold of Amayon while the building comes down around him, and when a teleport trap shakes him loose of the snake body it does not shake him loose of her. The Missing Piece quest opens on the back of it: free the demon, get him casting, and survive her totems for the ten minutes before she is back. She cannot be killed. That is not encouragement, it is a specification.

beats.headline: Put down by one of her own totems
beats.text: Goddess of Hopelessness and Insanity Ysalte has been removed from this realm by a totem raised from the former crawler Paz. Her own quest furniture, turned around and used on her. The Missing Piece completes. Elsewhere in the same collapse Crawler Carl rides his health down to five percent on purpose to set fire to every street he had walked on, which tells you what kind of afternoon this was for everybody.

beats.headline: Her crystal changes hands at the portals
beats.text: Crawler Osvaldo has been carrying Ysalte's memorial crystal since the ninth floor, on the grounds that his own god kept telling him it was the wrong one. He makes a run for the portals across a roof Crawler Carl has just opened up, and Crawler Britney stops him and takes the crystal. Samantha's assessment, delivered flatly: if Britney wants rid of Ysalte, she needs the Halls of the Ascendency or she needs Sheol, and neither of those is on this floor.

tagline.text: Taranis. A pig on a rival team is under his protection, which is a strange thing for a god of thunder to bother with.
Taranis, god of thunder. A crawler has worked out that the pig is the lever, and is holding a knife to it.
Taranis, god of thunder. Killed another god in an arena for taking a swing at a pig he loves.
Taranis, god of thunder. Killed a god over a pig, then walked out of the realm carrying two pieces of his mother.

beats.headline: The pig has a god
beats.text: Team One Fine Pig: two tigrans, Nico and Dario, in a throuple with a pig named Penelope. The interesting line in that file is not the throuple. It is that Penelope is under the protection of Taranis. A god of thunder has taken a personal interest in a pig on a racing team, and every crawler who reads that entry is going to file it somewhere and keep it.

beats.headline: Somebody found the lever
beats.text: The boss battle is on and Crawler Carl is spending his messages carefully. One goes to Emberus: I know who killed your son, meet me in the Scolopendra Club. The other is not a message so much as a hostage note. Taranis is in love with the pig. Carl says he will kill the pig if Taranis does not come and stop him. The god of thunder is now a scheduled arrival, and he was invited by threat.

beats.headline: He kills Emberus over the pig
beats.text: Emberus, pinned and made briefly vulnerable by two bolts from Princess Donut, swings at Crawler Carl. Penelope takes the hit instead, because of a Four-Leaf Clover Patch and the sort of luck this floor generates. Taranis kills him for it. A fire god, patron and quest-giver, removed from the arena inside a second by a thunder god defending a pig. I want everyone at home to appreciate the proportions here.

beats.headline: Two pieces of his mother
beats.text: Eris empties the arena's pockets and leaves. Khepri leaves. Taranis says he is taking two pieces of his mother with him, and goes, and what he takes with him is Samantha and Krakaren Prime. He does not explain the sentence. Nobody in the arena asks him to. I have the transcript and I have run it four times, and I am telling you exactly what he said and nothing more.

beats.headline: He takes the crystal on his way out
beats.text: Inventory note from the close of the boss battle. Prepotente's memorial crystal is gone, and Taranis took it. Crawler Carl finds a different one in the wreckage, made by a god dying in that arena, which is not the crystal anybody wanted and is the one that is left. The stairwells to the twelfth floor are open.

relations.note: Killed him in the arena
One of the two pieces he takes with him
Whose crystal he takes

tagline.text: Nekhebit. A crawler with a talk show has announced which deity she is sponsoring this season, and it is a name almost nobody in the audience recognised.
Nekhebit, the vulture goddess. A deity shouting through a portal says she is behind the corruption of the mother of all the gods.
Nekhebit, the vulture goddess. She has a champion now: a cat, three atrocities deep, wearing a class named for the tree that replaced her.
Nekhebit, the vulture goddess, last of the old gods. Bore three children she was forbidden, and one of them took her worshippers and her place.

beats.headline: Odette announces her sponsorship
beats.text: On her own show, in front of the audience she built, Crawler Odette announces that she is sponsoring a deity this season, and the deity is Nekhebit. Then she offers three choices of adjutant and Crawler Carl takes Baroness Victory. Everybody in the room is watching the adjutant question. I would gently suggest that the first sentence was the news.

beats.headline: What the crossbow says about her
beats.text: The lore attached to a repeating crossbow, for anyone who reads the flavour text: the long-forgotten goddess Nekhebit is jealous and terrible. When the elf mothers abandoned her to worship Apito, the Oak Goddess, Nekhebit grew enraged, blamed the male-dominated high elf court for letting her worshippers stray, and cursed their seed. Every elf and fairy breed in the universe traces back to that court and that curse. It is called the Fae Diaspora. Somebody put all of that on a weapon description and expected nobody to read it.

beats.headline: Named through a portal
beats.text: Hellik, holding a portal open with gods pouring out of it around him, uses the time he has to say four things to Crawler Carl. He did not kill Emberus's son. Everything Emberus believes about him is a lie. Apito has been corrupted. And Nekhebit, he believes, is behind all of it. A vulture goddess almost nobody down here had heard of two floors ago is now the name at the bottom of a divine accusation.

beats.headline: A champion, three atrocities in
beats.text: Crawler Princess Donut commits her third Atrocity and the system pays out: the Oak Fell class, and the title Champion of Nekhebit. Consider the shape of that. The class is named for felling the oak. The title belongs to the goddess the oak displaced. Somewhere above this floor an old grudge has just been handed a very small, very loud instrument.

beats.headline: Three children she was forbidden
beats.text: Rosetta tells the Scavenger story in the pet stables, where nothing above can hear it. Nekhebit was the last of the old gods and was forbidden to have children. She had three: Apito, Scolopendra, and a son. Apito defeated her and absorbed the worshippers she had left. Each of those three has been called the Scavenger somewhere in the myths, which is why nobody can agree who the Scavenger's Daughter is, and why the war mages keep looking at Samantha's daughter.

relations.note: Champion of Nekhebit
One of the three children she was forbidden

entities.name: Eileithyia

description.text: Eileithyia is something of an oddity. She's benevolent. Unlike most of these psychos, she's known for her kind heart. She's prayed to by all mothers, both when they're attempting to sow the seeds, and when the harvest comes. And while she does many things, she's mostly known as She Who Eases Pain. Both the physical pain of childbirth and the inevitable darkness that comes to those who are unable to complete their most sacred task. When the stillness comes, she is not the one who has caused the heartbreak. But she is the one holding the grieving mother's hand.

entities.voiceNote: A goddess who is genuinely kind, which makes her the strangest thing in this pantheon. Warm, plain, unhurried; she speaks to a crawler the way a midwife speaks to a frightened mother, practical and quiet, telling him exactly what to do next. Calls Carl by name. Talks about pain as something to be eased rather than paid for. Never threatens, never bargains upward, never raises her voice, and never says a word about what her sponsor wants.

tagline.text: I have walked into a realm where everyone assumes a god wants something. I do want something. I want a young woman and a cat to come out of this alive.
The favour I was promised in return did not arrive. I am honouring my half of it regardless, which everyone here finds astonishing.
I stood frozen while she chose which of my two doors to walk through. She took the one that sends her home pregnant, to help the children there. I would have chosen it too.

beats.headline: A quest about spiders, which is a cover
beats.text: I come in alongside Yemaya, wearing a sponsor from the Grixist Swarm, and the first thing I do is hand a floor boon to every crawler down here, because it costs me almost nothing and it is a kind thing to do. Then I give Carl's party a quest about spiders. The quest is a cover. What I want is to help him keep the two he is most afraid of losing, and the crown that is going to take them from him. So: accept the offer to be the team's adjutant. I will see that the votes fall the way they need to fall, and the protections come off the ninth floor, and the crown gets sorted. Tell nobody. Not the cat, not the woman making the offer, not your guide.

beats.headline: The flower with my name on it
beats.text: There is a flower in a thrice-sealed box with my name on it, and a doppelgänger has already broken two of the three seals to reach it. Whoever eats it takes a boon from me, and my boon has two shapes. She can be carried to the twelfth floor and stand as a celestial attendant until the games open. Or she can be made pregnant, and be pulled out of the crawl entirely, because I do not let anyone carrying a child fight in a place like this. Both are ways past the ninth floor without walking it. I did not put the flower in that box. I only decide what it does when she eats it.

beats.headline: The agreement stands
beats.text: The adjutant arrangement did not happen the way I laid it out. Odette is not the one in the chair. I find Carl in Florida and tell him plainly that this changes nothing on my side: what I said I would do, I am doing. He is waiting for the second half of the sentence, the part where I revise the price. There is no second half. Gods trade down here, and I am aware that this is what he thinks he is standing in. He is wrong, and I am not going to argue about it.

beats.headline: She chooses, and I take her out
beats.text: The doppelgänger wakes, and it is time, so I enter the realm. Then a cat casts Laundry Day on my sponsor and ejects her out of me, and I am held in place, unable to move a finger, until the choice is made. It is not a bad way to spend the minutes. Katia chooses to be pregnant, because there are children on the surface of her world and she means to help them. So I ease what needs easing, and I take her out of this dungeon, and her friends stand in the dust of a battlefield saying goodbye to somebody who is going to live.

relations.note: The adjutant offer she told him to accept
Her boon, and the door out

description.text: War God Grull. Level 250. Sponsored by Prince Maestro of the Skull Empire. Warning: This is a deity. He is invulnerable on this floor. This god has been involuntarily summoned to this location. Summoning rules apply.

tagline.text: Grull. A train engineer very nearly got his god into the room with a crawler party. Very nearly.
Grull, god of war, four storeys of him, driven by somebody who is thoroughly enjoying himself. Sent to the Abyss by a party that had no business surviving him.
Grull, god of war. Turned up in a factory the instant a broken puppet was made whole, because smiting is his department.
Grull, god of war. Level 250, invulnerable, and put down by a knight with a lance and a magnet.

beats.headline: A summoning barely avoided
beats.text: Gore-Gore, engineer, gives the party two routes back to the stairwell stations and then attacks them, which is the sequence I have come to expect from railway staff. In the middle of it he tries to bring in Grull. It does not land. Understand what almost happened there: a mob with a grudge and a prayer nearly put a war god into a train carriage with four crawlers. Horses pray to Grull. Centaurs pray to Grull. There are a great many horses on this floor.

beats.headline: Grull against the Mimic Rex
beats.text: Crawler Carl, a Mimic Rex, and War God Grull, in one place, and the god is being driven by the Maestro like a stolen vehicle. Grull kills the mimic. Grull steps on Carl. Carl's friends come for him anyway, which is the part I did not have odds on, and by the finish Grull has been sent to the Abyss. Four storeys of war god, removed from the floor by people who were, this morning, worried about a train.

beats.headline: What the file says about him
beats.text: The file, for those keeping one. Grull is one of the few trueborn heirs to the Celestial Ascendency, which makes him a candidate for the throne of heaven, and level 250, which makes him unkillable on this floor. His worshippers are horses, centaurs and tikbalangs, and from this floor down the llama-shaped ones join in as well. They paint themselves blue and talk without stopping about wenches and dying gloriously in battle. Crawler Carl's guide gave the blunt summary of the whole subject a long way back: there are no real gods down here, only the ones who pay for the privilege.

beats.headline: He arrives the moment the ritual works
beats.text: Crawler Carl drives a truck along walls and ceilings through dolls and slag elementals so that Grigori can finish a ritual, and the ritual works: Corky's two halves become one thing again. That is the good news, and it lasts about a second, because the instant it happens Grull enters the realm to smite him. Somebody up there was watching that ritual very closely and does not want it completed.

beats.headline: A lance, and a very large magnet
beats.text: Princess Donut casts Laundry Day and expels the sponsor riding Grull, which buys a moment. Grull goes for Corcunda instead, and Corcunda decides to take the smite himself so the others do not have to, and says so out loud to Dong, and Dong says he is not leaving him again. Then the two of them walk at a war god together. Donut puts Big-Ass Magnet on the lance, every screw in the factory comes with it, and Dong kills Grull with the lot. Grull goes back to the twelfth floor. The pair of them go back to the race, and make the line with seconds to spare.

description.text: Orthrus. Juvenile Gate Guardian. Level 10. This is a bereft pet of Geyrun. Who's a good boy? Who's a good boy? The most loveable hell-hound on this side of Alpha Centauri. The left side is for sniffin' and the right side is for lickin' and that pink belly of his? It's for kissin'.

tagline.text: Orthrus. Something very large is outside the bubbles taking the floor apart, and what it is looking for is a dog.
Orthrus. Two heads, floppy ears, roughly the size of a bubble, level 10, and not invulnerable the way the rest of them are. He is a puppy.
Orthrus. One quest says take the puppy home. Another pays crawlers for killing him. Both are live at the same time.
Orthrus. Hauled clear of a warzone by a man and a cat in an aeroplane, and collected by a god who wanted him back.

beats.headline: Something outside is looking for a dog
beats.text: Crawler Elle McGibbons reports in from a popped bubble: there is a deity outside, taking the landscape apart, and it is searching. Not hunting crawlers. Searching. The thing it has lost is called Orthrus. Nine hundred crawlers on this floor are currently working out how to survive a level ten hazard, and the largest event on my board is a god who has misplaced a pet.

beats.headline: He lands inside the bubble
beats.text: Orthrus is now inside the bubble with Crawler Carl's team, and everyone in there has been handed the Where the Red God Glows quest to go with him. Around the edges of it: two crawlers give their lives connecting an electric panel to free their quadrant, Maggie My gets out of her containment, and Princess Donut spends the whole thing trying to keep an enormous two-headed puppy alive. Everyone is very busy. Nobody is looking at the same emergency.

beats.headline: The one god down here who can die
beats.text: The file on him, since he is going to matter. Orthrus is a juvenile gate guardian, level 10, kid brother to the three-headed one who guards a stairwell exit a long way below this one. He was on course to become a vicious, baby-eating, nun-defiling murder machine, and then in a single day his master was murdered and he was pulled into the Nothing. Most things the Nothing touches come out ruined. He came out unaffected, because he is too innocent for it to take hold, and fire does nothing to him at all. Here is the line that matters to a crawler: unlike other gods, he is not invulnerable. He is a puppy. Happy, destructive, rambunctious, roly-poly, very pokey. Fragile.

beats.headline: Two quests, pointing opposite ways
beats.text: Crawler Carl and Crawler Princess Donut take an aeroplane up and use Meat Hooks, a spell built for hauling meat, to drag a puppy the size of a building out of the fighting. The quest that comes with it is simple: bring Orthrus to Emberus. Then a second quest is announced, and this one pays crawlers for killing him. Both are on the board together, which is a design decision somebody made and I am obliged to run. Crawler Quan Ch reads the second one and attacks the puppy.

beats.headline: Collected
beats.text: The aeroplane comes down with Quan Ch on top of Crawler Carl. Carl takes Emberus as his god mid-fall and throws a celestial grenade, the god arrives at his position, and for a short while nothing on this floor can touch him. Then Emberus finds Orthrus. The two of them go, together, and the floor is left to the people who were fighting over a dog.

relations.note: It touched him and did not take

tagline.text: Yarilo. A mage in a sandcastle wanted a love spell and aimed a summoning at this god. Something else answered, and the mage is still in the castle.
Yarilo, god of lust, feral now. Out of the Nothing and loose on a battlefield, chasing an AI who is very fast.
Yarilo, god of lust. Conscripted by an army that bought him with potions. Deities are inventory on this floor.

beats.headline: The summoning that went wrong
beats.text: Sandcastle of the Mad Dune Mage. Read Ghazi's description and the whole sad story is in it: he wanted the gate so he could summon Yarilo and have Yarilo make Lika love him. What came through was a different goddess entirely, who trapped him in this castle and married him to an ooze, and the real Lika is the soul-possessed doll frozen in the fountain that Mongo has just smashed. Crawlers, this is the standard outcome of aiming a summoning at a god of lust. Please make notes.

beats.headline: Why he is in the Nothing
beats.text: Since tonight's party runs under a peace seal, some history about the last god who broke one. At the first masquerade in the Halls, hosted by the mother of all the gods, Yarilo got drunk and forced himself on another deity's familiar. That broke the seal. Apito sent him into the Nothing for it, and he has been in the Nothing ever since. The seal on tonight's party is hers as well. Enjoy the canapes.

beats.headline: Out of the gate, chasing an AI
beats.text: Feral God Yarilo enters the realm and goes straight after Samantha, which is precisely what he was let out for: something enormous and single-minded, aimed at an AI who is fast enough to lead it wherever the crawlers want it to go. Meanwhile Katia Grim, Imani, Dong and a slugalette named Bigs join Carl and Elle at the Madness headquarters. Everyone has a job. Samantha's job is running.

beats.headline: Conscripted with potions
beats.text: The War Mage Rebellion has taken the Larracos castle and holds it for six hours to win, and they have gone shopping for reinforcements. They conscript Yarilo, paid for with potions they traded for the gate on the Midnight Market. Somewhere in that chain a god of lust became a line item. Fopsy has a theory about why Agatha is doing any of this, and I will let her explain it, because I have a god to move.

beats.headline: Taken off the board by another god
beats.text: Feral God Yarilo has been removed from this floor by Harpocrates, acting under the direction of Crawler Li Na. He came through a gate, chased an AI the length of a warzone, changed sides for a crate of potions, and finished at the hands of the god who had come through that same gate ahead of him. Everything down here becomes somebody's equipment, the gods included.

tagline.text: Meatus. First through the gate, into a war that was already going badly for everyone in it.
Meatus. Came through a gate into a war and picked a fight with the god who came through behind him.
Meatus. Reached into a pile of frozen witnesses and pulled a goddess in after him.
Meatus. Came through the gate first, fought the god behind him, and finished in pieces on a battlefield with the cameras looking away.

beats.headline: First through the gate
beats.text: Operation Ruin is written up in the cookbook, Princess Donut is installed in the Nest, and Crawler Elle McGibbons opens the Gate of the Feral Gods in Dream territory. What comes out first is Meatus. What comes out behind him is Harpocrates. Neither of them was requested by name, because that is not a thing the gate offers, and both of them are now on a floor with four armies on it.

beats.headline: He picks the other god
beats.text: Meatus and Harpocrates start fighting each other. Of every direction those two could have chosen on arrival, the crawlers have drawn the one that costs them nothing, which after the fortnight this floor has had feels less like luck and more like an apology. In Reaver territory the dwarves set off a volcano, so the ledger balances.

beats.headline: He pulls a goddess into the pile
beats.text: The pile of witnesses is frozen, conscious and invulnerable, which is a combination I would like on the record as not my idea. Princess Donut casts Rolling Battle Formation on the whole heap and starts it moving. Meatus reaches into it and drags Eris in with him. A goddess of discord, inside a rolling ball of frozen soldiers, on a battlefield. Somewhere the Party Planner is coming apart and Crawler Louis is falling into a castle, and it is still the second most interesting thing on this floor.

beats.headline: Chopped, and nobody watches
beats.text: Crawler Princess Donut casts War Crimes and Meatus comes apart into pieces. I closed the eye of the Scavenger's Daughter for that one, on the grounds that even she does not want to look at it, and I stand by the decision. Harpocrates swears revenge for him and leaves the realm. Two gods came through that gate. Neither of them is on this floor now.

relations.note: She opened the gate that brought him

description.text: God of Blacksmithery and Armor Ogun. Level 250. This god is not sponsored. Warning: This is a deity. He is invulnerable on this floor. This god has been temporarily summoned to this location. Summoning rules apply. He's here now because Ogun strongly believes all punishments should be handed out in person.

tagline.text: Ogun. Two crawlers get a quest from their own god, and it is not phrased as a request: fix my shrine, not theirs.
Ogun, god of blacksmiths. His shrine was not the one they picked, and he is coming into the realm about it.
Ogun, god of blacksmiths. Handed out a debuff nobody can heal, took a worshipper's life for a choice that worshipper did not make, and went home.

beats.headline: A quest from their own god
beats.text: Crawler Carl, Princess Donut, Paz, Anton and Sister Ines get themselves to Asojano's shrine intact, which required flagging a ghommid splitter named Skylar Spinach and a certain amount of nerve. Asojano begins a ritual. And in the middle of it, Paz and Anton receive a quest from Ogun, who is their god: only one shrine down here can be fixed, and he would like it to be his. Note the position those two men are now in. Note who put them in it.

beats.headline: The shrine they did not pick
beats.text: Deities appear from every direction, each of them making a case for their own shrine, which is the single worst committee meeting I have ever had to render. Then Katia Grim messages Carl: repair Yemaya's shrine or lose her and the cat to the Crown of the Sepsis Whore. So Bomo repairs Yemaya's. The ghommid settlement is freed, Carl walks away with slugpox and a card made out of Asojano, and Ogun enters the realm to punish his worshippers. Not the crawlers who chose. His own.

beats.headline: The outsider at the anvil
beats.text: The file, for the people about to meet him. Ogun is an outsider, one of the old gods, from an obscure pantheon that has dissipated into time, and until a minute ago he was the last surviving member of it. He spends his days at a celestial anvil, angrily making armour, piece after piece, and nobody knows why he does it or where the armour goes. It is said the pieces are a strange shape, all of them cut for four-legged beasts. He is a god of blacksmiths and armourers now. He was something considerably larger once, and his power and his ambition make him a real contender for the throne of heaven.

beats.headline: Punishment, in person
beats.text: Ogun puts a debuff on Paz that nothing down here can heal. Crawler Carl throws Black Nimbus over Anton to shield him, and Ogun kills Anton instead, and leaves the realm having taken exactly what he came for. Paz, going, spends his last minutes telling Carl and Donut two things about Sister Ines: her race makes everyone near her want to protect her, and it gets stronger the longer they are near her, and before the crawl she was a murderer. Sister Ines turns Paz into a card rather than lose him.

relations.note: The one who repaired the other shrine

entities.name: The Sledge

tagline.text: Seven feet of rock in a tuxedo. Me and Bomo work the door. The Princess calls me Sledgey.
Seven feet of rock in a tuxedo. Bought once at the bar, then written into a contract. I belong to her court now.
Seven feet of rock in a tuxedo. I got inside that castle, I cast Zerzura, and everything standing in it came away with me.

entities.voiceNote: Short flat sentences, one thought each, nothing decorated. Says the plain hard thing and then stops talking. The Princess, Bomo, Carl, Louis, all by name and nothing more. Never complains about a job, never explains himself, never refuses the Princess anything.

beats.headline: Bought at the bar
beats.text: Two crawlers come up to the counter and buy security. Me and Bomo, sold as the pair. That is the arrangement in this place. You pay, and we stand between you and whatever comes through the door. The cat is not what I expect. She orders a dirty Shirley in a bowl with extra cherries, drinks the whole thing, and then she wants dancing, so I do my version of the robot while she bops and twirls on my shoulders. Princess Donut. She calls me Sledgey. I let her.

beats.headline: A miss on his own shift
beats.text: A crawler goes for the Princess on my floor, on my shift, and I do not get there in time. Elle puts the second one down. Astrid comes to apologise in person, and I stand where I am and wait to hear what a miss like that costs a body like me. Carl does not ask for blood. He asks for me and Bomo, permanent and complimentary, the Royal Court's own security every time they walk in. So now I have a court.

beats.headline: Part of the price of the Gate
beats.text: Carl's lawyer trades the Gate of the Feral Gods back, and I am part of what he gets for it. Four of us, free of charge: me, Bomo, Clay-ton, Very Sullen. Two spells on top, one for Bomo and one for me, copies of what the artifact could do. Bomo gets the jump to the stairwell. I get Zerzura. Nobody explains Zerzura to me. Nobody has to.

beats.headline: Surviving is winning
beats.text: Louis is worried about how it is going. Whether the plan holds, how it looks, who comes out on top of it. Surviving is winning, Louis. Everything else is bullshit. Then the changelings and me go into that castle, through a turret and the elf inside it, which is the thing everyone outside said could not be done.

beats.headline: He finishes casting Zerzura
beats.text: The battle is everywhere and my job is to stand still and finish the words. So I stand still and finish the words. The castle goes. The whole building and every NPC breathing inside it, taken out from under the people who thought they owned them. That is what the spell was for. I said I did not need it explained.

entities.name: Astrid

tagline.text: Astrid. Bloodlust Sprite, level 125, assistant manager of the Desperado Club. Hand-sized, tuxedo, severe bun, and she can make your heart beat until it catches fire.
Astrid. Bloodlust Sprite, assistant manager, and none of that was the part worth knowing. Ask the two dancers crying in the strip club whose mother she was.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, not a voice. The System keeps the file on club management the way it keeps files on everything with a level: rank, class, capability, and what the record does not explain. Carl and Princess Donut are guests, Katia Grim is a contractor, and the club is the club.

beats.headline: The management apologises
beats.text: Astrid. Bloodlust Sprite, level 125, Cardiovascular Mage, assistant manager of the Desperado Club. The Bloodlust Sprite is one of the rarest and deadliest things her kind produces, born holding magic over anything with a circulatory system, and the signature trick is a heart beating fast enough to catch fire. She is the size of your hand, she wears a tuxedo, her hair is up in a bun, and her voice is deeper than yours. A crawler makes an attempt on Princess Donut on club grounds and Astrid comes down to say sorry in person. The Royal Court walks out with permanent complimentary security. Establishments like this one do not hand out refunds. She handed one out.

beats.headline: A contract on the management
beats.text: There is a job out on her, and Crawler Katia Grim has taken it. The preparation is thorough, which is the compliment: Samantha parked at the bar to make noise, Katia getting herself ready, Carl setting traps down the service corridor they expect the assistant manager to walk. Nobody in the building tells her. That is the arrangement everyone employed here works under, and she has known it longer than any of them.

beats.headline: She goes to meet the demon instead
beats.text: The distraction runs too hot, reaches the casino floor, and pulls Minge out of one of the doors to the Nothing. A minor feral demon on the premises during business hours. Astrid does not go anywhere near a service exit. She finds Carl, tells him she is releasing the Vorpals to put the thing down, and tells him to get everyone out. And while the floor empties she says two things she has never once put on record in all the years this club has been running: that she has children, and that her husband is the Night Wyrm.

beats.headline: The contract closes
beats.text: Astrid, assistant manager of the Desperado Club, is dead. Katia Grim joined Carl in the corridor and the two of them finished it there, and the body went back to the Night Wyrm to close out the contract he had put on it. On the way down she asked them to save her children. She also said that she was almost done. The Vorpals she had already released went and put the demon down without her, which is the sort of thing good management arranges in advance.

beats.headline: Whose mother she was
beats.text: Two of the dancers out of the Penis Parade are sitting in the strip club crying, and here is why. Damascus Steel and Anaconda are her sons. She and the Night Wyrm came into this place as crawlers, the same way Carl did, and never went home. Everything an assistant manager's influence is worth had been spent quietly, for years, keeping those two off the record and out of anyone's way. Her husband ordered the contract. Damascus wants every dancer in the Parade hired on as a mercenary where it is safe, and after that he wants his father.

entities.name: Ghazi

tagline.text: I am a glass mage. Transmutation, and the teleportation of energised particles. I came out to the sand to study a buried artifact, which is also what I told the College.
I am a glass mage. I opened a hole to ask a god for one small thing and something else came through it, and now everything I own is sand, myself very nearly included.

entities.voiceNote: Self-pitying and grandiose in the same breath; a scholar's vocabulary spent dressing up a want. Explains himself at enormous length to anyone in the room and blames the thing he summoned for what he chose. Lika by name, always. Never says the word coward, never mentions the lie he told the College unless cornered, never asks after anybody else.

beats.headline: What he wanted
beats.text: They come in through the fountain court, three of them and a dinosaur that shatters my Lika where she stands, and then they find me, so you may as well have all of it. Lika is a half-naiad trobairitz out of the stage plays they put on in the city. A bard cleric under a vow of celibacy, played by a different half-naiad every season, based on a minor deity, and not real. I know she is not real. I wanted Yarilo brought back out and asked to make her real, and to make her mine. I told the College of Magecraft I was studying the Gate of the Feral Gods for stable long-distance transport. What answered when I opened it was not Yarilo. It was something else that had learned to wear the name, and it is why this castle is what it is.

beats.headline: Married to the ooze
beats.text: She tricked me. That is the part I want written down. I asked for Lika and the thing married me to the ooze instead, and my wife is still down in my halls being exactly what she is. The doll in the fountain, the one with a soul sitting in it, that is the nearest thing to a real Lika this world ever managed. Carl knocks me flat and takes the winding box off me while I am out. I wake up with a headache and tell them everything anyway, because who else is there to tell.

beats.headline: Out of the castle, and no further
beats.text: Ghazi, human, level 43 glass mage, known across the quadrant as the Mad Dune Mage, is dead. The sand ooze went down, the sandcastle came in on itself, and Crawler Katia Grim carried him clear of it. She killed him in the open a moment after that, for the notes in his coat explaining how the artifact is worked. He went to sand. Carl and Princess Donut were still buried under the other end of the building and heard none of it.

entities.name: Henrik

tagline.text: Henrik. Principal of the Dromedarians at Hump Town, and the reason there is a man in the basement with pieces taken out of him. Except that it is not Henrik in there.
Henrik. Changeling, principal of Hump Town, one third of an artifact, and a body sitting in a flooded submarine.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, not a voice: the file on a man who is not the man, kept flat and procedural because the impersonation is the only interesting entry in it. Wynne, Carl, Princess Donut by name. The System does not speculate about which of the two of them the town liked better.

beats.headline: The basement under the town hall
beats.text: Hump Town's town hall, and a good number of the Dromedarian guards are not Dromedarians. In the basement is Wynne, held as collateral, and Wynne is willing to say who has been working on him. Henrik. Principal of the town, changeling underneath, level 50. What he wants out of Wynne is a spell that will put flesh on Quetzalcoatlus, and the method for getting it has been to take Wynne apart slowly enough that he might change his mind. Crawlers from the subterranean quadrant appear at the boundary and put Wynne down before any of it concludes.

beats.headline: He explains the collateral
beats.text: Carl and Princess Donut sit down with Henrik and he explains how collateral works here, which is the local economy in miniature: a body held against a promise, and the promise enforced by what may be done to the body. He is patient about it. He answers every question put to him. Then the tomb starts taking on water and the conversation is over.

beats.headline: The delegation to the gnomes
beats.text: The plan walks out of the hall in a line: Carl, Princess Donut, Firas, Louis, Katia Grim out of sight, a reanimated Wynne, and Henrik. They meet Leon, the Gnome Negotiator, and present Wynne as a man in urgent need of healing. Princess Donut offers to do the healing in exchange for passage onto the Wasteland. Leon will take three of them and no more: Wynne, the cat, and Carl. The rest of the delegation, changeling included, is left standing on the sand.

beats.headline: The body in the submarine
beats.text: Henrik of Hump Town, changeling, is dead, and has been for some time. Katia Grim runs into the flooded submarine to get away from a sharktopus, and Carl finds the body already sitting in there with its piece of the Gate of the Feral Gods still on it. One magically linked pocket watch, recovered. Also on him: a note recording that Quetzalcoatlus can be put down with an electric shock. Whatever else he was doing, he was still working that problem right up to the finish of him.

entities.name: Hellik

tagline.text: Hellik. God of sun and life, twin brother of Emberus, level 250, and the second half of what Carl signed for: a standing order to kill him.
Hellik. God of sun and life, twin of Emberus, and a great deal more civil in person than the quest attached to him suggests.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, not a voice. For most of the crawl this god is a red sun, a line on a quest log and a name on a hit list, so the page is the file rather than the man. Emberus is his brother, Carl is the acolyte, and the System declines to say which brother it believes.

beats.headline: The second quest
beats.text: Carl is an acolyte of Emberus now, and the paperwork comes with a brother attached. Hellik: god of sun and life, Emberus's twin, level 250, said around the celestial floors to be quite obsessed with killing his own brothers, and the likeliest hand behind Geyrun's death even though he was sitting in council with Emberus when it happened. Two quests arrive together with the acolyte's package. Find Out Who Killed My Son. Kill Hellik. The second one has a deadline attached and it is the twelfth floor.

beats.headline: The terms of a family feud
beats.text: What a god's grudge looks like when it is applied to one crawler. No magical item blessed by Hellik may be owned or used, so a whole category of loot is now dead weight. Every shrine of his is marked on the minimap. Every one of his adherents carries a symbol over their head and pays double experience when put down. The dungeon has been arranging this for a very long time and Carl has been in it for about six weeks.

beats.headline: It stops being paperwork
beats.text: NPCs who worship Hellik now go hostile toward Carl the moment they see him, no provocation and no conversation required. Inside Club Vanquisher the clerics stand in front of a stained glass door they will tell you shows Hellik bringing truth to Apito, whatever that is supposed to mean. It does not show Hellik at all. It shows the brother above him, and the clerics have had that door wrong for centuries.

beats.headline: He turns up in person
beats.text: The temple goes up, the portal starts letting gods through into Club Vanquisher, and Khepri comes out with the rest of them. Hellik banishes her on sight, in front of everyone. Then he turns to Carl with a message for his brother: he did not kill Emberus's son, everything Carl has been told about him is a lie, Apito has been corrupted, and Nekhebit is the hand behind all of it. He asks for an alliance. The quest to kill him is still open in Carl's log while he says it.

beats.headline: The clock on the order
beats.text: Quemada worships Emberus too, and Quemada's professional opinion is that the standing order cannot sit unattended much longer. They need to make an attempt on Hellik, and soon. Nobody in that conversation raises what Hellik said in the club.

entities.name: Quetzalcoatlus

tagline.text: A wailing shrieker over the tomb. She has no body, which is the whole of the problem for everybody who wants something out of her.
A wailing shrieker who guarded the tomb until two crawlers worked out where to put the wire.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, whole page. She is a guardian mob with no recorded conversation, so the file is what there is: what she is, what she can do, what people are prepared to do to a man in order to get it, and the four ways of putting her down.

beats.headline: A name out of a basement
beats.text: The name surfaces in a cellar under Hump Town, out of a man being taken apart in pieces. Wynne is being worked on to give up a spell, and the spell is meant to put flesh on Quetzalcoatlus. Whatever she is, she is worth a body to somebody, and somebody is prepared to do that to a man over several days in order to get her one.

beats.headline: Why the changelings want her flesh
beats.text: Juice Box lays out the arithmetic. The changelings want Quetzalcoatlus given a body so that they can touch her, because touching a thing is how a changeling adds it to the shapes it can wear. And they need what she carries: a great many of them are sick with compression sickness, and they believe she has a spell that alters living things which can be turned on the illness. A wailing shrieker over a tomb, wanted for her hands and for her medicine.

beats.headline: How to put her down
beats.text: A note comes off a body in the flooded submarine and it is the answer to her. Quetzalcoatlus can be finished with an electric shock. A wailing shrieker takes banishment, exorcism, a current, or the destruction of her lover's corpse, and of those four exactly one is lying around this quadrant with the power still running to it.

beats.headline: The panel in the tomb
beats.text: Quetzalcoatlus is finished. Morris and Low Thi drew her off and kept her occupied long enough to get the electric panel in the tomb connected, and the current did precisely what the note promised it would. Their quadrant is liberated and the bubble pops. Neither of them came back out of the tomb. That was the price the floor quoted, and the two of them paid it without renegotiating.

entities.name: Big Tina

tagline.text: Big Tina. Level 80 allosaurus, immortalized city boss, and the reason the dinosaurs keep coming down on Point Mongo.
Big Tina. Level 80 allosaurus, immortalized city boss, and an ursine child who never got to finish her solo.
Big Tina. Level 80 allosaurus, immortalized city boss, and a daughter with her mother standing in front of her.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, whole page. She is a city boss with no speech in the record, and the file the AI keeps on her is the only place her side of it exists at all. Kiwi is her mother, the recital is the wound, and the System reports the rage without recommending anyone go and test it.

beats.headline: The quest gets a name
beats.text: Samantha goes across the water to look at the far shore and finds the team over there dead. All of them, and all of them by one thing. The Recital quest updates with the name it has been withholding. Big Tina. Allosaurus, level 80, immortalized city boss, and the attacks on Point Mongo have been hers from the beginning.

beats.headline: Prepotente Town #4
beats.text: Carl and Princess Donut take two more towns and arrive at a third to claim it. There is not much left of the third. She has already been through it, and there is a pattern to which places she visits that nobody has sat down and read yet.

beats.headline: What she actually wants
beats.text: The party goes back into the town for Miriam and finds Big Tina standing in it again, and this time the shape of the thing comes clear. The dinosaurs of the Hunting Grounds were ursine before Scolopendra's nine-tier attack turned them into what they are. Tina was a child when it happened. What she wants, under all of it, is to dance at a recital, because hers was stopped before her turn came. She is also a vampire now, and she is building undead out of what she brings down.

beats.headline: She is brought in, and does nothing
beats.text: The dinosaur squad comes back to Carl and Princess Donut with Big Tina walking in behind them, and everybody in the clearing braces for the obvious. The obvious does not happen. Kiwi puts herself between the boss and the crawlers, and Tina stops. Nobody present can yet say why that works.

beats.headline: The recital, finally
beats.text: In the middle of the battle Princess Donut puts the I Take It All Back potion on Kiwi, and the pack leader is not a mongoliensis any more. An ursine stands there, heavily pregnant. Tina looks at her and knows her, and the Recital quest closes on the spot. It was never a quest about a monster. Nobody reading the log had any way of knowing that.

entities.name: Kiwi

tagline.text: Kiwi. Level 60 mongoliensis, head of an all-female raptor pack, and the reason nothing else does any hunting on this stretch of ground.
Kiwi. An ursine, heavily pregnant, and until about an hour ago the head of the fastest pack on the floor.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, whole page. A pack leader with no speech in the record, described the way the AI describes a mob it privately admires: raptor first, mother second, and the second one only once the record supports it. Mongo is the other dinosaur in the story and the System is not going to be delicate about that.

beats.headline: Mongo runs off
beats.text: Mongo bolts with Princess Donut still on his back and runs a pack of dinosaurs to ground. Kiwi is at the head of it. Level 60 mongoliensis, the fastest and cleverest predators anywhere in this jungle, and the whole pack is female, as is every dinosaur anyone has counted in the area. Which is odd. Odder still: dinosaur-class mobs did not exist on this ground before Scolopendra's nine-tier attack, and here they all are. Mongo and Kiwi settle the introductions between themselves, at length, with Princess Donut obliged to watch.

beats.headline: Charmed, and an escort
beats.text: Kiwi brings the pack in and Princess Donut charms her with a potion, and the fastest thing on the floor becomes an escort service. Carl works out at the same time that The Plenty arranged this entire chain of events, and that what it wanted out of the arrangement was Miriam gone.

beats.headline: She stands in front of a city boss
beats.text: The squad comes back to the crawlers with Big Tina walking in behind it. Big Tina is an immortalized city boss and everyone in the clearing understands exactly what that means for the next few seconds. Kiwi steps in front of her. Tina does not attack. Nobody yet has an explanation for it that they would put in writing.

beats.headline: Taken all the way back
beats.text: Mongo and Kiwi bring Vrah down together in the middle of the castle battle, which is a sentence worth reading twice. Then Princess Donut uses the I Take It All Back potion on her, and the mongoliensis is gone. An ursine stands in the wreckage, heavily pregnant, and Big Tina looks across at her and knows her mother's face.

beats.headline: Still pregnant, and family
beats.text: Kiwi is very pregnant and has been carrying since the Hunting Grounds, which is a long time to be in that condition even by this dungeon's standards. Big Tina, for her part, has decided that Mongo is her father. Nobody in the fortress has the standing, the courage, or frankly the desire to correct her.

entities.name: Edgar

tagline.text: Edgar. A giant tortoise who talks, and who puts the dead onto Signet's skin where they go on being useful.
Edgar. A giant tortoise who talks, and who can sit outside a building and tell you what is moving around inside it.

entities.voiceNote: Dossier, whole page. A tortoise with a specialist's skill set and almost nothing on the record in his own words, so the file lists the services instead: ink, reconnaissance, surgery. Signet's family, Carl's plan, Princess Donut's tattoo. The System does not make the obvious tortoise joke more than once.

beats.headline: The ink comes from the body
beats.text: Edgar is a tortoise. Edgar is also the reason Signet's tattoos are what they are, and the method is not squeamish: he works from the corpse. Miss Nadine, dead, goes onto Signet's skin as ink and comes back off it as something that moves and fights. Miss Nadine's attachment to Clint drags Clint along with her, so he turns up on the skin as well, unasked and unbilled. Nobody in the party looks surprised. There is apparently a queue for this.

beats.headline: He maps the castle from outside it
beats.text: Ahead of the castle job Edgar sits well back from the building and maps the whole of it from where he is. Every room, every level, and a set of small connecting tunnels that fit nothing anyone can name. Louis is the one who works out what they are for. They are Ferdinand's, so that he can move around his own house without ever using a door.

beats.headline: Sense Movement, level fifteen
beats.text: Rosetta has a theory about how Vinata keeps getting into Club Vanquisher, and Edgar is the instrument that settles it. He senses the non-corporeal moving through the castle. He also picks up upward momentum coming off the ground, which is what it looks like from below when somebody nearby worships a god for the first time.

beats.headline: A tattoo for the cat
beats.text: Rosetta, Milk and Edgar come up into the tower to work on Princess Donut. She is getting a tattoo, and given who does the ink around here, a tattoo is not decoration. It is a thing that will get up off her and fight when she calls it.

beats.headline: Surgery, on a clock
beats.text: Sixty-six minutes on the floor and every member of the party has a job. Edgar's job is surgery. He and Mordecai operate on Louis while the rest of it goes on above them, and nobody has told the tortoise how long he has.

entities.name: King Rust

tagline.text: King of the Skull Empire. My army is drawn up outside your walls and I have asked for a formal parlay. Do not read anything into that yet.
King of the Skull Empire. My daughter has taken one of my warships and told the Syndicate she intends to pull the switch on this planet with her own hands, and so I am here asking a crawler for help.

entities.voiceNote: A king accustomed to being obeyed who has just stopped being obeyed. Formal, blunt, ceremonial when ceremony serves him; the grief comes through the formality rather than around it. Crawler Carl, Princess Donut, my daughter, my empire. Never begs, never says please, never acknowledges how far the crying has already gone.

beats.headline: The army arrives, and asks to talk
beats.text: My army comes onto the field in good order, the way it has come onto every field for as long as there has been a Skull Empire. The crawlers seal their safe room against us, because they have learned what that doggy door of theirs is worth to an enemy. Fine. Let them shut it. I did not bring an army all this way to go through a door. I request an official parlay with Crawler Carl and Princess Donut, in the correct form, in front of every camera pointed at this floor.

beats.headline: The cat sees it first
beats.text: Baroness Victory reads out the rules of a parlay and each of us stands where we are told to stand. Deng Bao is at my shoulder, a Grixist, as an adjutant ought to be. Carl and the cat come out under the bubble and look at me, and the cat has it before a single word is spoken. I am crying. I have been a king a very long time and I have never once done this in front of an enemy.

beats.headline: What his daughter has done
beats.text: My daughter Formidable has commandeered one of my warships. She has announced to the Syndicate, openly, that she intends to trip the Failsafe by hand to keep the rogue thing on this planet out of the center system. And she told them the rest of it while she was at it: that my empire has been manufacturing their security systems with our own doors left quietly in the back of them. So here it is. I ask a crawler to send my daughter a message on behalf of the people of Earth, and I offer to pull my forces off this floor in exchange. Carl takes the deal.

beats.headline: Walking back to his own line
beats.text: King Rust of the Skull Empire is dead. The agreement was made and he turned to walk back to his own army, and Rosetta Thagra came out of where she had been waiting and took him, for reasons entirely her own and nothing whatever to do with the deal. His army attacked the instant he fell. His ring and his retina went onto a data pad in Rosetta's hands, Carl looted the body, and a parlay conducted in the correct form in front of every camera on the floor ended in the one way the rules had not covered.

entities.name: D'nadia

tagline.text: Princess of the Prism Kingdom. Small, as kingdoms go, and a considerable force in certain trade circles. I say what I think on air, and I have just watched them shoot my friend.
Empress now. I am judging a pet contest, which makes me part of the production, which is precisely why I am judging it.
I sponsored the cat. A sponsorship is an asset and I have sold the asset. Do not look at me like that. It is trade.
Warlord of the Prism clan. There is a crawler and a cat inside my castle, and everything I have done, I have done for my people.

entities.voiceNote: Warm, physically demonstrative, and blunt to the point of rudeness; trumpets through her facial tentacles when amused. Says 'the Prism Kingdom' in full whenever she is being official, which is often. Treats affection and trade as the same activity and has never noticed the difference. Never raises her voice at anyone she considers beneath answering.

beats.headline: A seat on the Danger Zone panel
beats.text: Ripper Wonton's panel, and the crawler and his cat are on it. I keep reaching for his hand and my claws keep going straight through his fingers, which does not stop me reaching. Then the Skull Empire fire at those two and hit Manasa instead. My friend. The comedian starts treating her death as a piece of political arithmetic, and I tell him to shut his mouth. The Prism Kingdom condemns the action, and I say so on air within the hour: we will bring a grievance against the Skull Empire in the Syndicate Courts.

beats.headline: Empress, judging the pet contest
beats.text: The ball, and I am judging the talent show and the pet contest both. Chaco is running the prize counter. I find the crawler in the crowd and tell him the truth of it: he and his attorney very nearly ruined my buy-in bid, and here I am regardless, judging, which makes me production.

beats.headline: Two places, bought
beats.text: Their team is on the board for the ninth floor. I will not pretend the cat's admirers managed that alone. Two places had to be bought, and I bought them, in my own name, where anybody watching could watch me do it.

beats.headline: The sponsorship changes hands
beats.text: I sell my sponsorship of Princess Donut to Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions. A waste company. They will want something for their money, and that is a matter between the cat and the waste company now.

beats.headline: Marked, and taken by the dinosaur
beats.text: Empress D'nadia of the Prism Kingdom, warlord of the Prism clan, is dead. Crawler Carl marked her with the Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering. Mongo did the rest.
