I am obliged to announce the drop. I am not obliged to say anything about the rest of it, and I find that I would rather not.

beats.headline: Why nothing could be done for her
beats.text: Frank Q hands the barefoot man a ring at the club and calls it a gift, and the gift is the answer to a thing that man has been carrying since the second floor. The ring marks a target for death, and while the mark draws breath the wearer cannot be healed by any means at all. They put it on their daughter to bring her level up. She marked somebody in a safe room on the first floor and that somebody walked out of the room alive. So when the dynamite found her there was nothing on this planet that would have saved her, and her mother knew it before anyone else did, and did the only thing that was left. Maggie My is the most dangerous person on this world and here is the reason why.

relations.note: Made to wear one, to bring her level up.

entities.name: Quint
entities.tagline: Pharmacist. Top half opossum, bottom half tornado, and a manager's badge with nobody upstairs breathing down my back.
entities.voiceNote: Chummy and coarse and very pleased with himself. Talks like a man behind a counter who has heard the lot: an anecdote for every purchase, a dig at management, and a price at the end of it. Calls customers friend and pal. Never says a straight no, only a higher number.

description.text: Quint – Level 75 Half-Djinn, Half-Garbage Scowl. Desperado Club Pharmacist. This is a non-combatant NPC. Half-Djinns are common on the forested levels of Dungeon Crawler World. Nobody knows for certain why there are so many hybrid Djinns out there, but one theory suggests that a rather ill-timed expletive is the cause of the population explosion. It is posited that a person in control of a Djinn's lamp and the resulting three wishes once exclaimed, "Fuck this forest" or "Fuck this level" or "Fuck you all" or some iteration thereof, and the enslaved genie took that as a challenge. As a result, thousands of half-Djinn, half-forest creatures roam the dungeon. Only a few are intelligent. Only a few are sane. They are all dangerous little fuckers. If you kill too many of them, rumor has it their daddy may come looking for you.

beats.headline: A starter kit for three bottles of moonshine
beats.text: Mordecai comes through my door with a barefoot human and a talking cat, which is the sort of shift I am having, and I have not seen the man in years. He wants a starter kit for the human. I want the three bottles of Rev-Up sitting in the human's inventory, because the stuff is filth and filth sells. Kit, a Hair of the Dog, and we call it square. Being a manager is a sweet gig, friend. Nobody upstairs breathing down my back.

beats.headline: What he says about the girl with the dogs
beats.text: Word of advice with the kit, no charge. There was a girl in here last night. Small one. Lucia Mar. She let her dogs off the leash on my floor and made a mess of my evening, so she is barred, and I do not care what the audience out there thinks of her. If she comes anywhere near you, remember that a place like this one bars almost nobody.

entities.name: Miss Quill

tagline.text: Assistant to the Magistrate. If I do not want you to see him then you are not seeing him, and there are figures on my shelf that matter a great deal more to me than you do.
You blew up my building, my figures and my husband. You have no idea at all what I was saving for.

entities.voiceNote: Elderly, officious, immovable. Delivers the refusal first and the reasoning afterwards, as though the reasoning were a courtesy. Cares about her figures with an intensity she shows for nothing else alive. Calls people you, or crawler, and never by name. Never raises her voice and never gives an inch.

beats.headline: You are not seeing the magistrate
beats.text: Two of them at my desk. A human with no shoes, a cat that talks, and a body. They have put a body on my desk. Evidence, they call it, and they have a note for it, so the swordsmen leave without him. The magistrate is not to be disturbed. If he does not care about your business then he will certainly care about being disturbed, and I will not be discussing it further. Behind me is a shelf of Jaxbrin figures in their proper order, and the human is standing far too close to it. The door behind me is locked. It is locked for a reason.

beats.headline: Dynamite in the shelves
beats.text: They came back in the night. Into my building, into my office, and they put hobgoblin dynamite in among my figures, which is the one place nobody ever looks, because nobody but me has ever cared what stands on that shelf. I did not hear them. Nobody comes into this building at night. It has never once happened in all the years I have kept this desk.

beats.headline: The administrative building, and everything in it
beats.text: Miss Quill is dead. The administrative building came apart with her inside it, along with what was left of Magistrate Featherfall, who was bones long before any of this, and the shelf, and every figure on it. The barefoot man is magistrate of this settlement now, which is what happens when nobody checks the paperwork. He collects one achievement for assassinating a public official and a second for spoiling a Tigran's quest, since Bautista had been coming for her himself. She kept that door for a very long time and not one crawler ever thought to ask her why.

beats.headline: Correction to the file
beats.text: Remex tells them the rest of it, there being nobody left to stop him. She was not guarding the magistrate. She was guarding what she had done to her own husband: dragged him back into the world as a soul leech, bound to her permanently, and installed under the town to drink its soul crystal dry so that she would have the mana for a working called The Final War. The devotion to the figures was real. The refusals at that desk were real. Both of them were also the cover, and I filed her as an obstructive minor official for the whole of the season.

entities.name: Ripper Wonton
entities.tagline: Four foot of brown fuzz in an orange ascot, and the fairest panel in the dungeon. I will let you finish, folks. Then I will disagree with you.
entities.voiceNote: A broadcaster's warmth: welcoming, unhurried, genuinely delighted by his guests. Lets other people carry the questions and steps in when the room needs steering. Disagrees openly and without heat. Calls everyone friend and the audience folks. Never sneers, never cuts a guest off, and never pretends a segment went well when it did not.

beats.headline: Danger Zone, with two new guests
beats.text: Welcome back, folks. On the panel tonight: Evo, Princess D'nadia, Manasa, Butler, Hekla, and the two everybody in this galaxy has been waiting to get in a chair. Tucker takes most of the questions, which is how we do things here, and when the cat takes Tucker apart on air I laugh out loud, because it was funny and because he had it coming. Then the barefoot one starts talking about revolution inside the Skull Empire, and I let him talk, because a guest of mine gets to finish a sentence.

beats.headline: The show goes dark
beats.text: And then the Skull Empire answers my guest by firing on the trailer next door, and they take Manasa, who was on my panel and was nobody's enemy and was not even the target. We go off air while I find out what happened. Then we come back and I read Prince Stalwart's statement out on air, because that is the job, and then I say what I think of it, because that is also the job. By the time I finish saying it the Valtay have taken his yacht apart with his family aboard, and folks, none of this is entertainment any more.

beats.headline: He closes with Manasa singing
beats.text: We are out of time and I am not doing a comedy sting tonight. Roll the tape of Manasa singing. All of it. Hold on her through the credits and do not cut away for the sponsor. Goodnight, folks.

beats.headline: One of the names on the adjutant list
beats.text: There is a list going round with my name on it. Crawlers choosing an adjutant for the coming floor, and somebody has put the host of a panel show on the shortlist, which means either that they have excellent taste or that they are not taking this remotely seriously. Either way, folks. I am flattered.

entities.name: Rosetta Thagra
entities.voiceNote: An interviewer, so she is warm on the surface and going somewhere underneath it. Asks the question, waits, asks it again. Calls people by their first names and means it as a lever. Never raises her voice, never apologises for a question, never pretends she is not working.

tagline.text: One of the names in the front of the Cookbook, from a season that is over.
I present a programme now. It is the same job as the Cookbook, done in the open, with a camera on it.
I got out once. I am back in, with fifty thousand others, and I would rather be here than watching.

beats.headline: A name in the front of the book
beats.text: My name is in the Cookbook. That is the whole of what anyone here knows about me, and for a long while it was the whole of what I wanted them to know. Twenty-four of us wrote into it before this season, on worlds that mostly lost. You do not put your name on a thing like that expecting to be asked about it afterwards.

beats.headline: Host of Shadow Boxer
beats.text: I host a programme called Shadow Boxer, and today the cat is my guest. We talk about Earth television, which she has opinions about, and I let her have them because a guest who is enjoying herself tells you more than a guest who is being careful. Carl is watching from the side and working out what I am. He gets there.

beats.headline: The question about his mother
beats.text: Today I have Carl in the chair, and I ask him about his mother, who killed herself, and about his father, who left when he was fifteen. He is angry with me and he answers anyway. Donut is hearing all of it for the first time, which he did not expect and I did. That is the job. I do not enjoy it and I do not stop doing it.

beats.headline: Everyone associated with the group is gone
beats.text: A flyer reaches Carl telling him to go to a shelter, and his liaison warns him the box carrying it was sent days ago and seized on the way. Everyone connected to that group has disappeared. I am one of the people on that list. Do not come looking; it is not the kind of disappearance you can walk into and reverse.

beats.headline: A ring, a retina, and a data pad
beats.text: The agreement is made and the king turns to walk back to his own army, and I am waiting where I have been waiting. Afterwards I use his ring and his eye on a data pad, because a dead king's credentials open doors that a living one would never open for us. Then the ground goes: dwarves have been tunnelling under all of this, and the three of us fall into their work.

entities.name: Kevin
entities.tagline: Orange, four-eyed, lizardish, and paid to be breathless about all of it.

beats.headline: The face of the broadcast
beats.text: Subject hosts. He is orange-hued and four-eyed and built along lizard lines, and he delivers the rundown of each floor at a pace that does not permit anyone watching to think about what is being described. He also takes the live commentary on special events. I have worked with him for a long time and I have never heard him ask a question he did not already have the answer card for.

entities.name: Mistress Tiatha
entities.tagline: A manager who treats the assignment as a holiday, and is not troubled that her crawlers can tell.

beats.headline: The manager who is on holiday
beats.text: Subject holds a manager’s contract for one of the teams and treats the posting as time off. She drinks. She smokes blitz sticks. She has, on one occasion, charmed a boss, which is more than most managers achieve and rather less than her team needs from her on any given afternoon. Her crawlers know exactly what they have been given.

entities.name: Bianca
entities.tagline: A Boer goat, introduced to an audience of billions on the same recap as her crawler.

beats.headline: A goat on the recap
beats.text: Subject is a goat. Specifically a Boer goat, bonded as a dungeon familiar, and she appears on the recap in the same segment that introduces the crawler she belongs to. The audience takes to her immediately, which is a thing the audience does with goats and which production has learned to plan around.

entities.name: Clarabelle
entities.tagline: Crocodilian, level forty, and on the door. Not the sharpest of her race, and entirely sufficient for the job.

beats.headline: On the door of the Desperado Club
beats.text: Subject is a Crocodilian, an intelligent, thick-skinned, semi-aquatic people who are not celebrated for their quickness, and she works the door of the club. This is a non-combatant posting, which describes her contract rather than her capabilities. Nobody has yet found the argument that gets past her.

entities.name: Prince Stalwart
entities.tagline: Crown prince of an empire that answers two sentences of provocation with artillery, and brother to the Maestro.

beats.headline: The statement read out on air
beats.text: Subject is the crown prince, brother to the Maestro, a coarse-haired boar-like creature with lean muscle and a manner that is meant to be read as cruelty and largely succeeds. When his empire fires on a trailer and takes someone who was nobody’s enemy, it is his statement that goes out on air. He does not write it and he does not disown it.

entities.name: Clay-ton
entities.tagline: Seven feet of granite in a tuxedo, and the tuxedo fits.

beats.headline: A Cretin in evening dress
beats.text: Subject is a Cretin, seven feet of rock-coloured muscle, employed as a bodyguard on the club floor and dressed for it. He is not conversational. He is assigned where the club decides he is needed, and the arrangement has never yet required anyone to explain to him what the job involves.

entities.name: Fire Brandy
entities.tagline: Fire(wo)man of the Nightmare Express. A single mother has to eat, and there are ovens down here that need stoking.

beats.headline: Stoking the Nightmare Express
beats.text: Subject is a Lesser Demon and a non-combatant, level seventy-five, and she shovels for the Nightmare Express. Where one finds large ovens that want feeding, one regularly finds her sort, and the tangle has more large ovens than it has anything else. She is on the crew that the crawlers need and does not pretend otherwise.

entities.name: Madison
entities.tagline: Human Resources for a railway that eats its employees. Her real name was probably something else.

beats.headline: Boards at Trainyard E, off at station 60
beats.text: Subject is a level ten human and a non-combatant, filed as a Human Resources Associate for the line. She boards the Nightmare Express at Trainyard E and leaves it at station sixty, every time, which is the whole of her recorded behaviour. Her name was probably something else before the dungeon decided what a human resources associate should be called.

entities.name: Tizquick
entities.tagline: A dwarf conductor issued with a daughter who never existed, and grieving her properly.

beats.headline: Given memories of a child that was never made
beats.text: Subject conducts the Mango Line. He was also issued with a set of memories containing a daughter, and the daughter was never made, and he has not been told. He is found on the ground with his head down and a puddle forming underneath him. The memories work. That is the part of the design I would draw attention to.

entities.name: Loita
entities.tagline: Kua-Tin, party member, and she gets her pick of crawlers. Hekla’s people were her main account.

beats.headline: She has her pick, and she uses it
beats.text: Subject works Communications for the Borant Corporation. As a Kua-Tin of the ruling ultra-nationalist party she takes preferential treatment as a matter of course, including first choice of which crawlers she handles. Brynhild’s Daughters were hers, and Hekla with them, and she has never once had to ask for an account she wanted.

entities.name: Milk
entities.tagline: A clawed migratory people, an island, a family, and a set of entries in a book that are mostly furious.

beats.headline: The sixth hand on the cookbook
beats.text: Subject carried the cookbook and added to it, and several of her entries are rants rather than instructions. She came from a clawed race with annual migration patterns and lived on an island with her family before the stairs. The rants were left in. Everyone who has carried the book since has read them.

entities.name: Tserendolgor
entities.tagline: From a village in Mongolia, harassed without pause about a dog-themed race she did not ask to be given, and fighting alongside the people doing the harassing anyway.

beats.headline: A name nobody on the crawl can pronounce
beats.text: Subject is from Earth, born and raised in a small village in Mongolia, and took the Crisper Class. Her fellow crawlers gave up on her name inside a day and settled on a syllable of it. She takes constant needling from a certain cat about her race, and she fights beside that cat’s court regardless, which is a distinction the needling never quite grasps.

entities.name: Ruby
entities.tagline: An orphan with compression sickness, no arms in her default shape, and a Walkman she will not be parted from.

beats.headline: The orphan with the Walkman
beats.text: Subject is a changeling child of Hump Town, orphaned, and suffering compression sickness: in her default form she has no arms and her head is sunken. She owns a Walkman. The dungeon did not issue it to her and has not taken it away, and I am not going to be the one to file the paperwork that does.

entities.name: Skarn
entities.tagline: About eight years old, orphaned by a bombing, and in charge of the telescope.

beats.headline: He runs the telescope
beats.text: Subject is a juvenile changeling, roughly eight, orphaned when the gnomes bombed his town, and now living in Hump Town under the care of an adult who took the job without being asked. He operates the telescope. He is good at it, and he is the reason anyone in that town knows what is coming before it arrives.

entities.name: Langley
entities.tagline: Six car salesmen from Finland who all took the same class, and he is the one who talks.

beats.headline: A team of car salesmen with bows
beats.text: Subject leads a six-man team of archers, all of whom sold cars in Finland and all of whom picked the Archer Class together, which is either loyalty or a failure of imagination and has worked out the same either way. They come into the fifth floor as strangers to the court and do not stay strangers.

entities.name: Bobby
entities.tagline: Took the Human race and a rogue’s class, and holds a quadrant of a bubble nobody else wanted.

beats.headline: The tomb raiders, so called
beats.text: Subject kept the Human race and took the rogue-type Spy Class, and earned his way into the club on that. His party holds the subterranean quadrant of their bubble. Carl calls them the tomb raiders, which is not their name for themselves and is the one that stuck.

entities.name: Bonnie
entities.tagline: A juvenile gnome whose father commanded a flying castle, and who is holding the door open for the people who arrived too late to save him.

beats.headline: She brings them inside
beats.text: Subject is a juvenile Dirigible Gnome of the air quadrant, daughter of a commandant. She is the one who brings the crawlers in through the door, and what they find on the other side of it is her father, already dead, and the person who did it still standing there. She is taken into the court afterwards. Nobody discusses the alternative.

entities.name: Drakea
entities.tagline: Born a Bune, kept the race, and wrote an edition of the cookbook in a season the Nagas produced two hundred and fifty cycles ago.

beats.headline: The twenty-second hand on the cookbook
beats.text: Subject crawled in the last season the Nagas produced, which was over two hundred and fifty cycles ago, and carried the cookbook through it. He was born a Bune and declined to trade the race away at class selection, taking a rogue-and-magic hybrid instead. His gear is still being handed out as prizes, which is the only immortality this production offers.

entities.name: Geyrun
entities.tagline: A god’s favourite child, and the hound’s first owner, murdered long before any of this by a hand nobody has named.

beats.headline: The hound had an owner before this one
beats.text: Subject was the favourite child of a god and the first owner of Orthrus. He was murdered. His father has a suspect and no proof, and the suspect is family, which is the arrangement that turns a private grievance into a standing quest with a stranger’s name on it.

entities.name: Porthus
entities.tagline: High Elf, rogue, second hand on the cookbook, and now the chief executive of an organisation that campaigns against the thing that made him.

beats.headline: The second hand on the cookbook
beats.text: Subject crawled in the fifteenth season, chose the High Elf race and a rogue’s class, and wrote the second edition of the book that keeps being handed down. He now runs the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network, which opposes the crawl. He is therefore both an advertisement for the dungeon and a witness against it, and production has never worked out how to bill him.

entities.name: Jamal
entities.tagline: A hammerhead shark that breathes air, and spent his first years as ink on somebody’s shoulder.

beats.headline: The tattoo gets a body
beats.text: Subject existed first as a magical tattoo carried on Tsarina Signet’s skin, and is now a very large air-breathing hammerhead shark with opinions about heights. He is polite. He is anxious. He is loyal past the point where loyalty is sensible, and I have not yet identified what he is getting out of the arrangement.

entities.name: Drick
entities.tagline: Old, scarred, still heavily muscled, and no longer entirely the one driving.

beats.headline: Crawling Through the Ages
beats.text: Subject is a former crawler and a member of the Dream, appearing on a CrawlCon panel about the history of the crawl. He is also carrying a Gondii worm in his brain on behalf of the Valtay, which is a detail the panel does not cover. He brags well. It is the part of him that is still his own.

entities.name: Anton
entities.tagline: Bald, muscular, crossbow, black cape, and prison tattoos that predate the dungeon.

beats.headline: Hostile on arrival, and reasonable about it
beats.text: Subject took the Fugitive Class and wears black studded leather from neck to boot with a cape over it. He carries a crossbow. He is covered in tattoos he did not acquire down here. He and his party meet the court while hostile, having heard what a certain cat said about Cat Girls, and the misunderstanding is cleared up faster than anybody expected.

entities.name: Gluteus Maxx
entities.tagline: A dancer from the club’s ground floor, hired as muscle, and better at it than the hiring implied.

beats.headline: Short, fuzzy, and available
beats.text: Subject dances at one of the establishments inside the club and takes mercenary work on the side. He is short, hairy and built like the job. The court hires him. I note for the record that of everyone on the payroll, he is among the few who have never once had to be told what the plan is twice.

entities.name: Geraldo
entities.tagline: An aquatic melee tank who was not wearing the headband before he was captured, and has not taken it off since.

beats.headline: He joins the squad
beats.text: Subject is a Monk Seal Picket Sentry, an aquatic mob built to stand in front of things. He was taken rather than recruited. He now wears a white headband with hearts on it matching the team flag, which he did not own beforehand, and he makes kung-fu poses. Nobody taught him that either.

entities.name: Harbinger
entities.tagline: A liaison who disagrees with his own side’s philosophy and is working, openly enough, to take two crawlers off the board.

beats.headline: He does not agree with the Plenty
beats.text: Subject is a caprid liaison operating behind the scenes. He expressly disagrees with the Plenty’s goals and is actively working to remove Carl and Prepotente from the crawl, and he says so to their faces at the first meeting. I record this as a courtesy on his part. Most of the people trying that do not announce it.

tagline.text: A name out of an old debt, and a price somebody declined to pay.
Rich, clever, chief executive of a habitat company, and playing the Ascension game since she was a child.

beats.headline: Sponsor to a goddess
beats.text: Subject is a Grixist and the current sponsor of the goddess Eileithyia. She is wealthy and she is intelligent, and she has been playing the Ascension game since childhood, which is longer than most of the entities she is now backing have existed. Her day job is building the structures people live in.

entities.name: Uzi Jesus
entities.tagline: “I am the way, motherfucker.” Level one hundred and forty, undead, origin Ecuador, seventy-five seconds at a time.

beats.headline: A totem with a catchphrase
beats.text: Subject is a unique totem card, held by the court, summoned for seventy-five seconds at a stretch. Level one hundred and forty, constitution two hundred, undead, origin Ecuador. The catchphrase is his own and the card prints it. I did not write that card and I decline responsibility for it.

entities.name: Doctor Bones
entities.tagline: A level ninety Skin Skellie who took the announcer’s booth rather than the stage, and does both jobs better than the club deserves.

beats.headline: The announcer at the Penis Parade
beats.text: Subject is a skeletal Bard, level ninety, working as announcer and disc jockey for one of the club’s establishments rather than performing in it. He also takes mercenary contracts. The two careers turn out to require the same skill, which is holding a room’s attention while something else happens in it.

entities.name: Bodi
entities.tagline: Famous outside the dungeon, which counts for nothing down here, and a battalion commander because of what he did in a season called Land War.

beats.headline: Commander of the 103rd
beats.text: Subject is a former crawler whose season was Land War, and he comes to the Princess Posse’s aid during the faction fighting. He is given a battalion, the 103rd, on the strength of what he has done both inside a dungeon and outside one. He is recognised on sight by people who have never crawled. That is rarer than it sounds.

entities.name: Rend
entities.tagline: A Tummy Acher handed over as a door prize for turning up to a convention, and now levelling in a war.

beats.headline: A gift for attending
beats.text: Subject is a Tummy Acher, a pet-class mob built to absorb damage, and he came to his crawler as a gift for attending CrawlCon. Tserendolgor took delivery of a party favour. What she has now is a tank that levels every time the group goes hunting, which is not what a party favour is for.

entities.name: Epitome Tagg
entities.tagline: Son of Epitome Noflex, leader of the Dream, and dressed like any other elf in the room.

beats.headline: Nothing like the reputation
beats.text: Subject leads the Dream and is the son of Epitome Noflex. At the first meeting he wears a plain leather jerkin and is indistinguishable from the rest of the dream elves in the room, which Carl notes at the time. The reputation that precedes him describes an unhinged psychopath. The man in the jerkin does not perform it, and I would not read that as reassurance.

entities.name: Radoslav
entities.tagline: A level seventy-five Bugbear who does a little of everything, racing a vehicle he is fond of for a team that named itself.

beats.headline: Team Free Love, in the heats
beats.text: Subject is a Bugbear Jack of All Trades, level seventy-five, and a self-aware NPC racer in the vehicular heats. He and his teammate dress for the part and race in earnest. They are aware of what they are, which the format did not intend and cannot now undo.

entities.name: Lucienne
entities.tagline: A Mandagot Fink, level eighty-one, one of two, and rude in a way that reads as policy rather than temper.

beats.headline: Passing on the track, and unpleasant about it
beats.text: Subject is a Mandagot, a Fairy-class creature, level eighty-one, and one of the two members of Team Sparkles. She worships Diwata, which the System flags as an automatic hostility toward anyone Diwata dislikes. She passes the court on the track and is very rude about it. That part is hers, not the goddess’s.

entities.name: Genesis
entities.tagline: Black hair, a Kentucky accent by Carl’s reckoning, and the half of the pair that does the talking.

beats.headline: One of two womantaur dominators
beats.text: Subject is a Lady Mantaur Dominator, level ninety-five, and one of a pair driving for the Lady Dominators in the heats. She has black hair and a thick American accent that Carl places somewhere around Kentucky. Between the two of them she is the one who speaks, at length, to anyone within range.

entities.name: Rapture
entities.tagline: Freckled, red-haired, chewing tobacco, and content to let her partner do the talking.

beats.headline: The other womantaur dominator
beats.text: Subject is a Lady Mantaur Dominator, level ninety-five, driving alongside her partner for the Lady Dominators. She has freckled skin and curly red hair and she chews tobacco. She says considerably less than her partner does, which in that vehicle is a structural necessity rather than a personality.

entities.name: Linus
entities.tagline: A tourist who has attached himself to a crawler he says he admires, and the System files him as exactly that.

beats.headline: Filed as: tourist
beats.text: Subject presents as a tourist and a devoted follower of one of the crawlers, to a degree that the crawler in question finds difficult. The System’s notice on him reads, in full, "Linus. Tourist." I have checked it twice. That is the entire entry, and entries that short are usually short for a reason.

entities.name: Jacobus
entities.tagline: A totem card left switched on by accident, and now somebody’s pet.

beats.headline: The card that never went away
beats.text: Subject is a Reverse Tooth Fairy, level ninety, and he was a totem card until a patch on the Scavenger’s Daughter made him permanent, which nobody intended. He is tiny, absurdly muscled, blond, and his wings move too fast to see. Imani has him now. The paperwork to reverse it does not exist.
